beats.what: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize went to Navi Pillay, a South African judge and former UN human rights chief.
beats.why: She spent decades making sure war crimes get punished through international courts.

cards.body: On Friday in Oslo, the Norwegian Nobel Committee gave the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay. She's a South African lawyer and judge who spent decades making sure war crimes actually get punished. The committee said she pushed peace through international law.
That's 208 people and 79 organisations. Only one name won.
cards.caption: candidates nominated this year

cards.body: Big crimes in wars, like genocide (trying to wipe out a whole group of people), often go unpunished. Pillay worked as a judge at international courts that put people on trial for them. The idea: if leaders know they can be punished, they think twice.
cards.title: why does a judge get a peace prize?

cards.body: Lowkey a desi W: Pillay is of Indian Tamil origin. Her family's roots go back to India, even though she was born and built her career in South Africa. Also, this is a guaranteed GK question in your next competitive exam.
The committee couldn't reach her before announcing it. The chair said live on stage that if she saw a Norwegian number calling, she should "please pick up."

a.body: The committee says international law is now an "absolute necessity" for peace. Trials make it harder for leaders to commit war crimes and walk away.
a.label: Supporters say

b.body: Critics often point out that big powers can ignore these courts, and trials come years after the damage is done.
b.label: Sceptics say

cards.note: US President Trump has repeatedly said he deserves this prize.
cards.title: Do international courts actually stop wars?

cards.q: Which of these did Pillay serve on as a judge?
cards.why: She was a judge at the international tribunal for Rwanda, and later at the International Criminal Court.

opts: Punish war crimes, that's how you stop the next one
cards.q: Should the Peace Prize go to people who end wars, or people who punish war crimes?

hook: Who just won the Nobel Peace Prize? (Spoiler: *not Trump*)
